status: DRAFT — not frozen. Freeze only after a blind planning-Critic red-team on the host that runs it.
purpose: Solution-option EVALUATION + DESIGN + SYNTHESIS + CURATION. Consumes the terminated output of Programme A (an option set) and produces a DECISION-READY DOSSIER for the engineer. It does NOT merge, does NOT choose, and does NOT ship.
preconditions: Programme A has terminated and produced >=2 candidate options. If only 1 candidate exists there is nothing to curate — run /bk-codexreview on it instead.
Every candidate is identified by an immutable ref (branch@sha), never by branch name alone — branch names move.
A dirty tree or protected branch refuses at preflight; run --review-only if the tree cannot be cleaned.

slice_rule_when_evidence_is_branches.problem: Programme A's candidates COLLIDE by construction — three writers editing the same three files. Slicing by FILE is therefore impossible: the slices would overlap 100% and fake corroboration.
slice_rule_when_evidence_is_branches.rule: Slice by CANDIDATE, one candidate per blind builder. Builder-i sees ONLY candidate-i's diff vs the merge-base, plus the shared rubric. It never sees a sibling candidate.
slice_rule_when_evidence_is_branches.why_this_preserves_blindness: Disjointness is over EVIDENCE, not over questions. Three builders answering the SAME rubric questions against THREE different diffs is the cleanest possible partition: identical lens, disjoint evidence.
slice_rule_when_evidence_is_branches.anti_anchoring: A builder that saw a rival diff would grade relative to it. Per-candidate blindness forces each candidate to be graded on its own merits against a fixed rubric, which is what makes the scores comparable at merge time.
slice_rule_when_evidence_is_branches.materialisation: Do NOT hand a builder a live branch (it can git-log its way to the siblings). Materialise each candidate as a static diff artifact vs the common merge-base, write it to its own directory, and cite that path as the slice source.
slice_rule_when_evidence_is_branches.shared_context_is_allowed: The merge-base tree is shared by all three slices. That is legitimate — it is the COMMON BASELINE, not contested evidence. Declare it explicitly in the manifest description so the independence audit is not surprised by it.

elements.text: Every candidate is scored on the SAME fixed rubric, each dimension 0-5 with the score justified by an exact file:line citation from that candidate's own diff: (a) correctness of the state transition it introduces; (b) test evidence carried WITH the change (count assertions, not files); (c) blast radius = files touched outside the scheduler package; (d) reversibility — can it be reverted as one commit; (e) conformance to the canonical stage list and to existing op-type/schema contracts; (f) observability — does it make its own failure loud, or can it fail silently.

For each candidate, state what it does that the others CANNOT do — the unique capability lost if this candidate is discarded. This is the salvage list and it is the single most important output of the run: it converts a 3-way either/or into an explicit inventory of what a synthesis must preserve.

For each candidate, state its DEFECTS as an adopted baseline: what would have to be fixed after adoption. Cite lines. A candidate with no stated defects is under-examined, not perfect — the Critic must REFUTE any all-clean scorecard.

Collision map: for every file touched by more than one candidate, record the hunks that overlap and classify each as (i) trivially reconcilable, (ii) semantically conflicting — two different designs for the same behaviour, or (iii) mutually exclusive. Class (ii) and (iii) are what make this a curation decision rather than a merge.

SYNTHESIS candidate: is there a composition that takes the salvage list (B2) from all candidates and satisfies the collision map (B4)? Describe it as a concrete change plan against the merge-base. If no synthesis is possible, say so explicitly and state which capability must be sacrificed — never silently drop one.
Max 20 scored claims per builder plus ONE consolidated 'what my candidate cannot tell me' block of at most 6 bullets, which does not count against the ceiling.

CURATION IS AN ENGINEER DECISION. The run's terminal artifact is a decision-ready dossier: scorecards, salvage list, collision map, synthesis option, and a RECOMMENDATION with its dissent recorded. The recommendation is advisory. The run MUST emit the choice as an open ESCALATE and MUST NOT merge, rebase, cherry-pick, close or delete any candidate. Discarding two lanes' work is not an agent's call.

Negative-evidence rule: 'candidate X does not handle Y' requires a citation of where it WOULD have to appear plus evidence of absence (a grep that returns nothing, quoted). Unsupported absence claims are rejected at adjudication — absence of proof is the easiest way to smear a rival candidate.

The Critic is seated NON-BLIND across all candidates, because comparison is precisely the non-blind task. It receives all three scorecards plus the collision map and must (a) re-score any dimension where two builders applied the rubric inconsistently, (b) name any scorecard that is internally incoherent, (c) adjudicate the synthesis option adversarially. Prefer the cross-provider codex Critic; degrade to Claude LOUDLY with a recorded reduced-independence warning, never silently.

DEPLOYABILITY across repos and hosts: for the recommended option, what must be true for it to reach every lane — is it release-gated, does it need a version bump, does each host need a redeploy, and does any host pin a version that would not receive it? A remediation that lands only on the authoring host has not been deployed, and this element exists because that has already happened repeatedly.

What NEW silent-failure surface does the recommended option introduce? Every remediation in this problem domain has so far been a silent-failure fix that itself failed silently. Require an explicit answer, including how the change announces its own malfunction.

questions: Which candidate is the best ADOPTION BASELINE, on cited rubric evidence rather than on size or recency?
What must be salvaged from the candidates NOT adopted, and is a synthesis that preserves it feasible?
What does adoption cost across every repo and host, and which lanes would silently not receive it?
Which parts of this decision are genuinely the engineer's, and what does each option foreclose?

run_directions.invocation: buildkit-3rtask preflight --task-type plan --subject '<the curation question, as a REFERENCE not pasted diffs>' --manifest <candidates.json> --builders 3 --min-cycles 2 --max-cycles 3 --token-budget <N> [--review-only]
run_directions.subject_must_be_size_invariant: The subject names the candidates by branch@sha and points at the dossier. NEVER paste diff bodies into the subject — 359,474 insertions on one candidate would overflow the context window. The BRIEF carries names; the BUILDER reads its own diff from its slice path.
run_directions.critic: codex (cross-provider) strongly preferred here. The Critic is adjudicating between lanes' work; same-provider self-adjudication on a contested curation is the weakest possible configuration.
run_directions.cycles: min 2. Cycle 1 scores candidates; cycle 2 re-examines specifically the dimensions the Critic re-scored and tests the synthesis option, which usually does not exist until cycle 1 has produced the salvage list.
run_directions.freeze_order: Curator freeze happens BEFORE any /bk-codexreview delegation. Reason: codexreview reviews a DIFF for defects; it has no opinion on which of three rival designs should exist. Sequence: Programme B freezes the chosen design -> the design is implemented -> /bk-codexreview reviews that implementation. Delegating to codexreview first asks a code reviewer to make a portfolio decision, which it will answer confidently and wrongly.
run_directions.composition_with_programme_A: A terminates when the option set stops growing (loop-until-dry, not a fixed count). Its output — the option set with provenance — IS B's manifest input. Do not re-run A to feed B; if A terminated, its option set is the input. Re-running A re-discovers the same options and costs a cycle.

hard_refusals: Never merge, rebase, cherry-pick, force-push, close or delete a candidate branch.
Never resolve the curation ESCALATE inside the run — record the engineer's stated resolution only.
Never write into another lane's board or repo to enact the outcome.
